icp: Hermes Agent users who switch dangerous-command approval policy across CLI, TUI, desktop, gateway, and cron surfaces
pain: Approval-mode ownership is split across shared command logic and TUI gateway helpers, increasing the chance that valid values, effective readback, or managed-policy behavior drift by surface.
revenueHypothesis: A single tested approval-mode contract reduces security regressions and maintenance time in the Hermes runtime used to deliver Helix revenue products.
mvpAcceptance: The valid approval modes and effective-mode read path have one shared owner used by the cross-surface command and TUI gateway.
Existing manual, smart, and off behavior remains unchanged across CLI, gateway, and TUI config reads.
Focused approval command, gateway, approval parity, and TUI gateway tests pass without weakening or deleting assertions.
The branch is clean, committed, pushed to origin, and independently reviewed against the exact commit.
rollback: Revert the single approval-mode refactor commit or reset the task branch to base commit 474b7e3579ff16226aaa8d4abf9600a2da5867b4; the active Hermes install and live config remain untouched during development.
stopConditions: Stop on approval behavior change, managed-policy bypass, prompt-cache mutation, unrelated source edits, secret exposure, more than two implementation attempts, or any focused regression test that cannot pass without weakening it.

vercel.exceptionReason: Hermes approval policy is part of the local Python runtime and TUI/desktop backend, not a Vercel-hosted web application.
